title: The 60-Second Pitch
sub: The hallway at CELA. You're not closing — you're earning a meeting. One clean minute, then a specific ask.

title: Four beats
displayText: Memorize the shape, not a paragraph.
note: HOOK — the pain in one line · WHAT — one3seven in a sentence · PROOF — the one credible detail · ASK — a specific next step.

title: The 60-second version
say: You know the 90-minute intake where someone rebuilds a worker's whole file by hand? one3seven flips that — the worker organizes their own employment record, every fact linked to its source, and sends it to your firm already organized. You open a clean, verifiable file instead of a shoebox.

title: Make it concrete and small
displayText: Not “are you interested?” — that invites a no.
say: Could I set you up with a firm code to try it on one real intake this month?
note: A specific, low-cost yes. Then stop talking and let them answer.

title: The 3-minute expansion
displayText: Expand only where they showed interest.
note: Add Coverage Rate (how much of what the law requires is on file) · worker-owns-it (why it's not a referral service) · the honest line: we use AI to organize, but every fact is source-linked.

title: The do-nots
displayText: A cold pitch is where people oversell.
never: It scores/picks the best cases for you. / You'll win. / Here's the price…
say: Don't score, don't promise outcomes, don't name a price in a hallway, don't run past 60 seconds.

title: A firm code. One intake. This month.
sub: Hook, what, proof, ask — then silence. Small, specific, clean. Now go start a conversation.
